leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eleven round 1 files (the chair's own included) name B011 as the preferred single part, and all six now propose the same two laureates, Nobuhiro Kiyotaki and John Moore. Enflo, Hjalmarsson and Stromberg moved from an opening three-name proposal that included Mark Gertler to two names; the other three held two names throughout. Shared: the originating 1997 mechanism (collateral values and credit limits feeding back on each other), its age of nearly three decades, and a narrow citation wording. Not shared: how much weight the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises should carry. Hjalmarsson and Stromberg treat the 2022 overlap as a wording issue, while Andersson, Enflo, Hassler and Krusell list it among their main reservations. The six also disagree on how the Gertler/Gilchrist accelerator strand should be handled. Several of them list the indirect empirical identification of the collateral channel as an open weakness. Every B011 supporter lists this, and every one of the six also records the 2022 overlap as an uncertainty. A file counts only for its own explicit preference; opening first-place counts are not treated as evidence of merit.

Three files prefer B005 (Elhanan Helpman and Marc Melitz). Boppart and Fredriksson moved to it in round 1 from B001 and B019 respectively; Friberg ranked it first at the opening. Shared: Melitz (2003) is the central model, Helpman's credit rests on the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple and related firm-level work, the framework has more than twenty years of firm-level confirmation, and Redding is left out of a two-name award. Shared reservations: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited, Krugman's 2008 prize overlaps with Helpman's earlier work, and some welfare conclusions depend on functional form. The three differ on wording. Friberg and Boppart would anchor the citation on selection and reallocation across firms, and Friberg also raises a Melitz-centred credit as an option. B005 is the preferred part or a listed alternative in ten of eleven files; Hjalmarsson is the exception.

One file (Teorell) prefers B012 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley). The case: it founded a formal and empirical field on how constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity shape fiscal policy, and it differs in object from the 2024 institutions prize. Teorell concedes that cross-country identification (regime coding, reverse causation), dispersion across many contributors, and his own field adjacency are weaknesses, and he now regards B005 and B011 as having cleaner attribution. Enflo, Fredriksson and Stromberg list B012 as an alternative, and none of them ranks it above their own first choice.

One file (Dreber-Almenberg) prefers B014 with Autor, Hanson and Katz, citing transparent, long-scrutinised designs and replication of the skill-premium findings. Acknowledged weaknesses: the task-based and trade-shock strands may be two achievements, Acemoglu and Restrepo are outside the credited names, and the magnitude and persistence of the China-shock effects are still debated. Hjalmarsson lists B014 as her first alternative. The third-name choice is open: Katz in Dreber's, Hjalmarsson's and several opening proposals, Dorn in the chair's opening proposal, and Krusell's opening proposal names only Autor and Hanson.

areas_of_agreement: B011 and B005 are the two candidates that nearly all files treat as serious. B011 is the preferred part or a listed alternative in all eleven files, and B005 in ten of eleven.

Both leading candidates are regarded as mature: roughly three decades for Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) and more than two decades for Melitz (2003). Members treat B001 (Mian-Sufi) and B026 (mobility with administrative data) as younger, with confirmation still accumulating.
No file supports a three-name B011. All six B011 supporters now propose Kiyotaki and Moore only, and Boppart, who prefers B005, also says he would not add a third name to B011.
For B005, every file that addresses the third name leaves Redding out of a Helpman-Melitz pairing.

Several files say a citation should be worded narrowly: the collateral-price mechanism for B011, and the theory of firm heterogeneity and selection, not the whole empirical firm-trade literature, for B005.
Members say explicitly that opening first-place and top-three counts are not evidence of merit and that the substance should be re-argued.
scientific_disputes: Identification of the collateral channel. Several B011 supporters accept that the channel is established more as a mechanism and modelling building block than as a measured magnitude. Boppart, Dreber-Almenberg, Fredriksson and Friberg treat the more direct firm-level testing of B005, or the replication record of B014, as a real advantage. Hassler and Stromberg argue that the prize can recognise a theoretical mechanism whose implications have been examined in many settings.

Whether the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig) covers collateral-based amplification. Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell and Stromberg read it as distinct ground. Fredriksson says the overlap weighs more heavily with her. Andersson, Enflo and Dreber-Almenberg list it as a live reservation, and Teorell says his opening concern was answered.

How B001 (Mian-Sufi) relates to B011. Hassler and Krusell describe Kiyotaki-Moore as the general mechanism and Mian-Sufi as a well-identified application to household credit. Boppart opened with B001 first, then moved away from it in round 1 because of its recency and the unsettled weight of credit supply versus other housing-boom explanations.

Whether the B005 welfare conclusions are robust. Boppart, Fredriksson and Friberg flag sensitivity to functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity and CES demand, while accepting that the core selection mechanism is robust.
B012: how much of the case rests on theory and later state-capacity work, as opposed to early cross-country regressions with endogeneity and coding problems (Teorell, Fredriksson, Friberg, Enflo).
B014: whether the task-based and trade-shock literatures are one achievement or two, and whether the China-shock effects are persistent (Dreber-Almenberg, Hjalmarsson).
attribution_disputes: B011: Gertler (and possibly Gilchrist) are excluded by all six supporters, who hold that the financial-accelerator strand is a different mechanism, is entangled with the work recognised in 2022, and splits Gertler's credit with B019. Enflo, Hjalmarsson and Stromberg earlier proposed Gertler as a third name. Andersson, Enflo, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell and Stromberg all list the Gertler/Gilchrist boundary as an open uncertainty, and Hjalmarsson and Stromberg say they would not object if the committee decided otherwise.

B005: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited, and Krugman's 2008 prize covers earlier monopolistic-competition trade theory. Members differ on how much marginal credit Helpman has. Several (Hassler, Krusell, Enflo, Dreber-Almenberg) treat this as a reason to prefer B011 on attribution grounds. Boppart, Fredriksson and Friberg regard it as manageable through wording. Helpman's separate B020 entry (protection for sale) adds a boundary question.

B019 (New Keynesian framework): eight credited names against a three-laureate limit. Krusell and Fredriksson both say any trio omits major contributors. Fredriksson has moved off B019 for now and would revisit it if a defensible selection existed.
B014: third name (Katz or Dorn; Krusell proposes only Autor and Hanson) and the task-framework credit that sits partly with Acemoglu and Restrepo.
B012: whether three names capture a dispersed field, and the Besley/Persson/Tabellini composition (Teorell, Enflo, Friberg).
maturity_disputes: B011 is regarded as mature by its supporters. The remaining maturity question is the relevance of the 2022 recognition, not the age of the idea.
B001 (about a decade old): the weight of credit supply is still debated. It appears as an alternative only in Hassler's file, and Boppart now lists it second among his alternatives.
B026 (mobility with administrative data) has a shorter confirmation record and relies on restricted data (Hjalmarsson). Only Hjalmarsson lists it as an alternative.
B014: the debate over the size and persistence of China-shock effects may change the long-run reading. Dreber-Almenberg sees the qualitative conclusion as surviving ten years of scrutiny.
B012 is three decades old, but its recognition may be pre-empted if the committee reads it as part of the same theme as the 2024 institutions prize. Teorell and Enflo argue it is distinct.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair (Hassler): I am a preferred-B011 supporter and also write this summary. I co-author frequently with Krusell (secretary, also a B011 supporter) and with Boppart and Friberg (both B005 supporters). No connection to Kiyotaki, Moore, Helpman, Melitz or any other credited name on the leading entries is shown in my profile.

Boppart: discloses co-authorship with Krusell and Hassler, a long collaboration with Peter Klenow (credited in B016, not in his preferred configuration) and work with Aghion, Bergeaud and Li. He notes no tie to Helpman, Melitz or Redding.

Friberg: discloses co-authorship with Hassler and Ellingsen, field adjacency to B005 and to B034, and a family relationship to a Swedish politician stated as a public fact. He reports no tie to a credited name and no evidence that the relationship bears on his assessment.
Krusell: discloses long-standing co-authorship with Hassler and Boppart and an adjacent field to B011. He reports no tie to Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler or Gilchrist.
Teorell: discloses that his field is adjacent to B012 and that he may overrate it. He reports no tie to Persson, Tabellini or Besley.

Fredriksson and Teorell both refer to a remark by Stromberg about Persson's past committee role (B012). That remark does not appear in the Stromberg round 1 file I have, so I cannot assess it. Conflicts are disclosed, not adjudicated.

Hjalmarsson (labour and crime economics, adjacent to B014 and B026) and Andersson (microeconomic theory and market design, adjacent to B048) disclose field proximity only, with no personal connection.
questions_for_round2: B005 supporters (Boppart, Fredriksson, Friberg): what evidence or wording would resolve your concern about B011's 2022 overlap and indirect identification? Please also state whether you would support a two-name B011 if the citation clearly separated collateral-price feedback from bank-focused and accelerator work.

B011 supporters: does your preference survive the strongest B005 attribution objection? Specifically, which of the issues (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum; Krugman 2008; Helpman's separate entry) would you treat as decisive against B005 and which are manageable through wording?

Can the committee draft a candidate citation for B011 and one for B005 that make clear what is not being honoured (the accelerator strand; the empirical exporter-premia facts)? Please propose specific wording.

Is a Melitz-centred single-credit option for B005 more defensible than the Helpman-Melitz pair? Please state Helpman's marginal credit independently of Krugman's 2008 recognition and independently of B020.

Teorell and Dreber-Almenberg: if your preferred part cannot reach the six-vote requirement, which listed alternative would you support in a single-part prize? Hjalmarsson, which alternative (B014, B026) would you support if B011 does not carry?
Does anyone see a coherent two-part pairing under the three-laureate limit, as Enflo, Boppart and Friberg say they could not find? If not, is a single part the working assumption for round 2?
Fredriksson, Krusell and others: is there any defensible three-name selection for B019 that resolves the eight-name attribution problem, or should B019 be set aside for this round?
summary.chair_observation: Based only on explicit round 1 files, B011 has six preferred-part positions, which equals the six-vote requirement. B005 has three, B012 one and B014 one. The count includes my own position and that of a frequent co-author (Krusell), and all six B011 supporters list the 2022 overlap and indirect identification among their reservations, so the lead is narrow and not a finding of merit. B005 is the preferred part or a listed alternative in ten of eleven files and is the main competing configuration, with the dispute turning on attribution and the 2022 overlap more than on scientific quality. Round 2 should focus on these two comparisons and on citation wording.
